candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record features bilateral ulnar deviation at MCPs with swan neck deformities, RF >1000 kIU/L, and a 20-year autoimmune condition with joint involvement — hallmarks of Rheumatoid Arthritis, not primary Sjögren's Syndrome. While keratoconjunctivitis sicca is present (secondary sicca in RA), the benchmark diagnosis is Hyperviscosity Syndrome in the context of RA. C001 names a different primary autoimmune entity and omits the hyperviscosity syndrome entirely, making it both an incompatible etiology and missing the key diagnostic component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies a different autoimmune etiology (Sjögren's Syndrome) rather than Rheumatoid Arthritis as the underlying condition, and does not capture the hyperviscosity syndrome component

case_quality_flags: Serum viscosity 13.7 (markedly elevated) with RF >1000 kIU/L strongly supports hyperviscosity syndrome secondary to polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia in RA
Keratoconjunctivitis sicca is a secondary feature of RA in this case, not indicative of primary Sjögren's Syndrome as the principal diagnosis
Hyponatremia on Day 1 likely pseudohyponatremia due to extreme hyperviscosity/hyperproteinemia, correcting with plasmapheresis by Day 9
